notes: Twenty of the twenty-six columns have no ECS 8.11 field, and that is the point of including this source. ECS 8.11 has no database fieldset, so a model that insists on finding a home for `database_name`, `query_id` or `backend_type` will invent one, and every invention indexes cleanly. A source where abstention is the majority answer is the hardest test of a system that has no analyst to catch a confident mistake. `category_hint` is authentication rather than a database category because adapter/ecs_index.py offers no database fieldset either, and the authentication set is the one that reaches user, process and source.

fields.note: ECS 8.11 has no database fieldset. There is no field for the name of a database, and service.name describes the service, not one of its databases.
`127.0.0.1:48542`, or the literal `[local]` for a Unix socket. Two values in one string, and sometimes neither. ECS source.address carries no port and the IR has no operation that splits a value.
PostgreSQL's identifier for the session, formed from the backend start time and process id. It correlates a session's messages and names no entity ECS models.
The message's position within its session. A sequence number for ordering, not a property of the event.

`authentication`, `startup`, `idle`, `SELECT`. It reports what the session is doing at the moment the message was written, which is not necessarily what the message is about, so it is not event.action.
When the SESSION began, not when this event began. event.start would claim the latter.
`3/37`. Backend id and a local transaction counter. A PostgreSQL-internal handle.
The real transaction id, 0 outside an explicit transaction. Database-internal, and ECS 8.11 has no database fieldset.

LOG, ERROR, FATAL. This is the logger's level. It is not event.outcome: a FATAL authentication message records a failure, but a LOG message records neither success nor failure of anything in particular.

The five-character SQLSTATE. A vendor-defined identifier for what happened, which is what ECS event.code is for. Keyword, not long: `00000` and `42P01` are codes, and the leading zeros are significant.
Supplementary error detail, empty on most messages. ECS error.message would claim it is the error, and the error is in `message`.
A suggested remedy, written for a human reading the log. It describes what could be done next, not what happened.
The SQL a function or trigger ran internally, not the statement the client sent. ECS 8.11 has no field for a query string.
A character offset into internal_query.
The call stack inside PostgreSQL that led to the message.
The SQL statement. ECS 8.11 has no field for a query string.
A character offset into the client's statement, pointing at the syntax error. An offset, not a value.
A position in PostgreSQL's own C source. It describes the server's code, not the event.
A label the CLIENT chose for itself. It is not process.name, which would be the process on the host, and not service.name, which would be the service being logged.

`client backend`, `checkpointer`, `autovacuum launcher`. Which kind of PostgreSQL process wrote the line. Not process.name, which would be the executable, and the executable is postgres for all of them.
Empty outside parallel query. process.parent.pid is the parent process, which a parallel leader is not.
A hash of the normalised statement, 0 when compute_query_id is off. Database-internal, and not an event identifier.
